anomaly_def.Name: Database Memory Allocation Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly : Excessive growth of buffer caches, work areas, session heaps, or other in-memory regions pushes the database process and operating system beyond safe physical or virtual memory limits.
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly : Free space for data files, logs, temp segments, backups, or diagnostic areas is exhausted, causing allocation failures and write stalls.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly : Listener, socket, or network-path limitations prevent timely creation and servicing of client connections and data transfer.

When all three conditions coexist, the database exhibits a multilayer resource crisis: memory pressure triggers aggressive paging and swap I/O that rapidly depletes disk space; simultaneous log, temp, or swap growth collides with already scarce storage capacity, producing "out of space" errors, stalled checkpoints, and frozen DML. As space and memory related stalls lengthen response times, client sessions linger, connection pools retry, and partially opened or slow-draining sockets accumulate, overwhelming listener backlogs and exhausting server process slots. Administrators may observe a vicious cycle of rising resident-set size, skyrocketing swap usage, temp-space allocation failures, exploding archive/log volumes, surging connection timeouts, and cascading instance restarts or cluster failovers.

Causally, unbounded memory allocations provoke paging; paging writes inflate swap and temp files, accelerating storage consumption. Once disks fill, swap expansion and log growth halt, amplifying memory faults and forcing abrupt process terminations that leave orphaned TCP sessions. The mounting queue of stuck or retried clients sustains high connection counts, each reserving additional memory and socket buffers, further tightening the memory squeeze. Conversely, network slowdowns prolong transaction and bulk-load durations, keeping large result sets, work areas, and temp segments alive and growing, which hastens both memory and space exhaustion. The intertwined feedback loops among memory, storage, and connectivity thus reinforce each other, rapidly degrading overall database availability and making root-cause isolation difficult.

entry.official_definition: Maximum amount of time allowed to complete client authentication; if not completed in time, the server closes the connection.
entry.trigger_condition: A would-be client does not complete the authentication protocol within authentication_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The server closes the connection attempt, preventing hung clients from occupying a connection indefinitely.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
